reason: H0 never creates or destroys an ares_channel_t, so S1's changed locking and event-thread/configuration teardown behavior in ares_destroy is unreachable. However, ares_destroy was already entirely unreachable under S0 + H0; the commit only adds internal ares__channel_lock/ares__channel_unlock calls and adjusts synchronization around existing teardown. It neither changes H0's parser APIs nor introduces a new externally controllable protocol, so it does not introduce or materially aggravate the pre-existing coverage gap.
evidence: H0 calls only ares_parse_*_reply functions and corresponding ares_free_hostent/ares_free_data cleanup functions.
H0 contains no call to ares_destroy and constructs no ares_channel_t.
The S0 -> S1 diff changes only ares_destroy.
The added behavior is ares__channel_lock(channel) and ares__channel_unlock(channel) around the existing ARES_OPT_EVENT_THREAD/configchg teardown.
The pre-existing ares_destroy body already depended on channel state including optmask, reinit_thread, all_queries, and event-thread teardown, none of which H0 controls.
recommended_action: No commit-specific harness maintenance is required. A separate channel-lifecycle harness exercising ares_destroy with ARES_OPT_EVENT_THREAD and relevant teardown state could address the historical gap independently.
